purpose: Peginterferon beta-1a is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows down the progression of physical disability. It does not cure MS, but it can help manage the disease and keep symptoms from getting worse as quickly.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes mistakenly attacks the protective covering around your nerve fibers, which is what causes MS symptoms. Peginterferon beta-1a is a man-made version of a natural protein called interferon beta that your body already produces. It works by calming down this overactive immune response, helping to protect your nerves from being damaged.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills, body aches, and fatigue, especially after your injection. You may also notice redness, swelling, or soreness at the injection site. These flu-like symptoms often get better over time, and your doctor may suggest taking over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen to help.
warnings: This medication can sometimes cause serious liver problems, so your doctor will monitor your liver with blood tests. It may also lower your blood cell counts, making it harder for your body to fight infections or stop bleeding. Tell your doctor right away if you feel very sad, hopeless, or have thoughts of harming yourself, as this medicine can sometimes affect mood. Do not use this medication if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: Peginterferon beta-1a is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once every 2 weeks. You will likely start with a lower dose and gradually increase it over the first few weeks to help your body adjust. Your healthcare team will show you how to inject it yourself at home using an autoinjector pen or prefilled syringe.
